# Become the Gold Digger You Wish to See in the World
- URL: https://www.notliketheothergolddiggers.com/become-the-gold-digger-you-wish-to-see-in-the-world/
- Published: 2026-07-25T20:09:44.000Z
- Description: I've also lived, and voluntarily left, the life some of you bitches are holding seances to summon.
- Author: Kara Hobby, Jackson Hole, Wyoming

Romance is dead. The dating pool is toxic, the apps are a wasteland, and the discourse about all three is somehow worse than any of it. Whatever! I don't care anymore.

From brokeys to billionaires, I've dated across the full economic spectrum.

I've said "wow, babe" with an inhuman level of enthusiasm over mediocre accomplishments. I've listened to business ideas that were neither businesses nor ideas.

I've also lived, and voluntarily left, the life some of you bitches are holding seances to summon.

Men want an equal partner who pays half, does everything, needs nothing, stays beautiful, and never develops the vulgar habit of expecting anything in return.

The only variable is whether you walk away with real estate or a prescription for Lexapro.

Never again. It's time to put yourself first. It's time for self-care.

**Where da gold at???**

And yes, sweetie, self-care can absolutely include power of attorney.

### Prioritize Your Peace

You cannot show up as your best self while splitting a check.

When the bill arrives, go deaf, blind, and dumb. Sit in the discomfort. Stay strong.

Do not reach for your purse. Do not perform the little fake search. Do not say, "Should we?"

We should absolutely not!

### Communicate Your Needs

A healthy relationship depends on honesty, so be honest. Use "I" statements:

- *"I feel unsafe when I am not on the deed."*
- *"I feel unseen when your life insurance policy still lists your sister."*
- *"I feel unsupported when your accountant keeps asking who I am and how I got into his office."*

Men cannot read minds. Be specific.

Do not say, "I need more commitment." Say, "I need you to love me in a language I understand: beneficiary designations."

### Make Time for Yourself

You cannot pour from an empty cup. Fill yours with pursuits whose only purpose is to generate invoices.

Consulting. Art advisory. Brand strategy. A non-profit foundation with vague goals and unusually high administrative fees.

You do not need to master these things. Mastery is not the point. The point is remaining open, curious, and extremely expensive.

Your interests may change. That is growth. Your monthly allowance should not. That is a boundary.

### Protect Your Energy

Not everyone deserves access to you. Access is earned through consistency, generosity, wire transfers, and gifts that can be independently appraised.

Stop overextending yourself for men who have done nothing to demonstrate emotional availability, financial solvency, or a willingness to add your name to the title.

Wellness culture loves telling women to "hold space." Absolutely. Hold space on his AmEx until the statement balance looks like an international phone number.

Protecting your energy may mean silencing notifications. It may mean declining invitations. It may mean placing several assets into a shell company before his family becomes suspicious.

### Release What No Longer Serves You

Sometimes growth means letting go. Let go of resentment. Let go of guilt. Let go of the belief that his adult children need to be informed before major financial decisions.

You will hear objections:

*"That is his kidney."*

*"That is a legally binding document."*

*"She has quite obviously forged my signature."*

These are fear-based statements.

### Know When to Walk Away

Leaving is not failure. Sometimes it is the bravest thing a woman can do...after the wire transfer clears.

Do not remain somewhere you are merely tolerated. With love in your heart and deep gratitude for the lessons, go where you are celebrated, protected, and listed as the sole beneficiary of an irrevocable trust.

You are not cold. You are *healed*.

You are not materialistic. You are finally choosing *yourself*.

**Love is for poor people.**

# Woman Who Chooses Lower Ground
- URL: https://www.notliketheothergolddiggers.com/woman-who-chooses-lower-ground/
- Published: 2026-08-14T03:44:19.000Z
- Description: It began as most of my best decisions do: with spite.
- Author: Kara Hobby, Jackson Hole, Wyoming

As America’s self-designated number-one hiking hater, I have always considered myself an exceptional steward of public lands mainly by refusing to set foot on them.

Living in Jackson Hole means you are surrounded by extreme athletes so constantly that you eventually forget what normal people do for fun. You hear “mild scramble” enough times and start thinking, *Well, how bad could it really be?*

It began as most of my best decisions do: with spite.

Last summer I announced I was going to climb the Grand Teton. A friend laughed out loud. Everyone else assumed I was joking.

That was all it took. Suddenly I was off to the races like a thoroughbred fueled purely by pettiness.

I was not new to hiking. I spent a good chunk of my early twenties trekking around western Washington, which is how I came by my hatred honestly. I love nature. That is why I live out West surrounded by it every day. I just do not see why admiring it needs to be so aggressively labor-intensive.

Yet suddenly I was grinding up Snow King every other day. I took up running, and if you know me at all you know I despise running. I was even willing to risk the dreaded "runner’s face."

My strategy with heights had always been simple: do not look down. If I do not look down, the drop does not exist. This works great on chairlifts.

I am here to report that this does not work when you are climbing and forced to look at your feet because directly beneath your boots is thousands of feet of sheer empty air.

Some people feel completely at home up there. I know people who casually free-solo the Grand before lunch. This fascinates me in roughly the same way it would fascinate me to meet someone who can be set on fire without feeling pain. They genuinely love it. I do not and I never will.

At 8:43 a.m. I reached the Black Dike at around 12,400 feet. I had hiked nearly seven miles and felt strong. But when I laid eyes on the actual vertical rock face ahead of me, a dark clarity washed over.

![Kara Hobby in a black cowboy hat, unimpressed](https://storage.ghost.io/c/48/6a/486a924e-e8e1-4b1d-9ccf-33d11c4615a2/content/images/2026/10/kara-hobby-cowboy-hat_o.gif)

I began running the risk-versus-reward calculation. Then I stopped and thought: *Wait… what is my reward here exactly?*

![From Kara Hobby’s Grand Teton climb: a dark fantasy tower under storm clouds](https://storage.ghost.io/c/48/6a/486a924e-e8e1-4b1d-9ccf-33d11c4615a2/content/images/2026/08/data-src-image-d9703b82-9d6d-4a39-bbd0-28139eeac6d1.jpeg)

My fingers were swollen to twice their normal size, actively being strangled by rings I had forgotten to take off. I was getting woozy. My brain was lagging.

It was me versus me, and for once both of us unanimously agreed this was idiotic.

So I made the executive call: *I’m out this bitch.*

Hallelujah.

I will never forget the euphoric high of turning around to head home. What a filthy, unadulterated joy it was to strut downhill while everyone else was still slogging up. Descending has always been the best part of any hike, but this time was pure triumph.

When an extreme athlete dies on a mountain, people always comfort themselves with the same line: *“At least they died doing what they loved.”*

What were they going to say about me?

*“Tragic. She died doing the exact thing she never shut up about hating.”*

Absolutely not. If I am going to die doing something reckless, I had better at least be having a good time.

![From Kara Hobby’s Grand Teton climb: a woman in pink sunglasses at a fashion show holding a sign that reads "At least you tried hoe"](https://storage.ghost.io/c/48/6a/486a924e-e8e1-4b1d-9ccf-33d11c4615a2/content/images/2026/08/data-src-image-17fa429c-19cf-4f4b-858f-56ef4b13c335.jpeg)

I trained for months because I wanted to know if I could do it. Standing at 12,400 feet, I decided that "probably" was close enough.

I thought this journey might turn me into *Woman Who Climbs Mountains*.

It did not.

I am proudly *Woman Who Chooses Lower Ground*, and she lives to hate hiking another day.

![From Kara Hobby’s Grand Teton climb: interview headline "I don’t want to be in a situation for even an hour where I’m not enjoying myself"](https://storage.ghost.io/c/48/6a/486a924e-e8e1-4b1d-9ccf-33d11c4615a2/content/images/2026/08/data-src-image-daede7a3-0ad9-4847-b4ea-7bff7b56e9f8.jpeg)

![XOX Love, Kara](<base64String>)
